passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home and you present an offering made by fire to the LORD from the herd or flock to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD—either a burnt offering or a sacrifice, for a special vow or freewill offering or appointed feast— then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, “Tell the Israelites this message.
You will enter the land I am giving you as your home.
When you enter this land, you will present offerings to the LORD.
You will make offerings by fire to the LORD.
You may offer a burnt offering or a sacrifice.
You may offer these for a special vow, a freewill offering, or at your appointed feasts.
You will offer these from your herd or your flock.
These offerings will make a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The person who brings an offering to the LORD must also bring a grain offering.
The grain offering must be a tenth of an ephah of fine flour.
Mix the flour with a quarter of a hin of olive oil.
Present this grain offering with your sacrifice to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם כִּ֣י תָבֹ֗אוּ אֶל־ אֶ֙רֶץ֙ מוֹשְׁבֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֖י נֹתֵ֥ן לָכֶֽם׃ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֨ם אִשֶּׁ֤ה לַֽיהוָה֙ עֹלָ֣ה אוֹ־ זֶ֔בַח לְפַלֵּא־ נֶ֙דֶר֙ א֣וֹ בִנְדָבָ֔ה א֖וֹ בְּמֹעֲדֵיכֶ֑ם לַעֲשׂ֞וֹת רֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה מִן־ הַבָּקָ֖ר א֥וֹ מִן־ הַצֹּֽאן׃ וְהִקְרִ֛יב הַמַּקְרִ֥יב קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ לַֽיהוָ֑ה מִנְחָה֙ סֹ֣לֶת עִשָּׂר֔וֹן בָּל֕וּל בִּרְבִעִ֥ית הַהִ֖ין שָֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions to Moses for the Israelites.
God told them how to bring offerings after they entered the land He would give them.
If you offer a lamb as a burnt offering or a sacrifice to God,
you must also prepare a drink offering.
You must use wine for the drink offering.
You must measure a quarter of a hin of wine.
You must pour this wine with the lamb offering.
passages.original: וְיַ֤יִן לַנֶּ֙סֶךְ֙ רְבִיעִ֣ית הַהִ֔ין תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה עַל־ הָעֹלָ֖ה א֣וֹ לַזָּ֑בַח לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָֽד׃

passages.text: With a ram you are to prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil, and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions for the Israelites.
God told them what to do when they bring offerings.
If you offer a ram to the Lord, you must also bring a grain offering.
The grain offering must be two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour.
Mix the flour with a third of a hin of olive oil.
You must also bring a drink offering.
The drink offering must be a third of a hin of wine.
These offerings will make a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
passages.original: א֤וֹ לָאַ֙יִל֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מִנְחָ֔ה סֹ֖לֶת שְׁנֵ֣י עֶשְׂרֹנִ֑ים בְּלוּלָ֥ה בַשֶּׁ֖מֶן שְׁלִשִׁ֥ית הַהִֽין׃ וְיַ֥יִן לַנֶּ֖סֶךְ שְׁלִשִׁ֣ית הַהִ֑ין תַּקְרִ֥יב רֵֽיחַ־ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD, present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil.
passages.sermon:
The LORD gave instructions for offerings.
You may offer a young bull to the LORD.
You may offer the bull as a burnt offering.
You may offer the bull as a sacrifice to fulfill a vow.
You may offer the bull as a peace offering.
With the young bull, you must also bring a grain offering.
The grain offering must be three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour.
Mix the fine flour with half a hin of olive oil.
Present the grain offering with the bull.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ תַעֲשֶׂ֥ה בֶן־ בָּקָ֖ר עֹלָ֣ה אוֹ־ זָ֑בַח לְפַלֵּא־ נֶ֥דֶר אֽוֹ־ שְׁלָמִ֖ים לַֽיהוָֽה׃ וְהִקְרִ֤יב עַל־ בֶּן־ הַבָּקָר֙ מִנְחָ֔ה סֹ֖לֶת שְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה עֶשְׂרֹנִ֑ים בָּל֥וּל בַּשֶּׁ֖מֶן חֲצִ֥י הַהִֽין׃

passages.text: Also present half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
You must present half a hin of wine.
You must use this wine as a drink offering.
You must offer it by fire.
This offering gives a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: וְיַ֛יִן תַּקְרִ֥יב לַנֶּ֖סֶךְ חֲצִ֣י הַהִ֑ין אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for offerings.
These instructions apply to animals used for sacrifice.
Follow these steps for each animal.
Do this for every bull.
Do this for every ram.
Do this for every lamb from the sheep.
Do this for every goat.
passages.original: כָּ֣כָה יֵעָשֶׂ֗ה לַשּׁוֹר֙ הָֽאֶחָ֔ד א֖וֹ לָאַ֣יִל הָאֶחָ֑ד אֽוֹ־ לַשֶּׂ֥ה בַכְּבָשִׂ֖ים א֥וֹ בָעִזִּֽים׃

passages.text: This is how you must prepare each one, no matter how many.
passages.sermon:
God gave instructions for offerings.
\r\nYou must prepare each offering in the same way.
\r\nIt does not matter how many offerings you bring.
\r\nPrepare each one according to these instructions.
passages.original: כַּמִּסְפָּ֖ר אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּעֲשׂ֑וּ כָּ֛כָה תַּעֲשׂ֥וּ לָאֶחָ֖ד כְּמִסְפָּרָֽם׃

passages.text: Everyone who is native-born shall prepare these things in this way when he presents an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A native-born person belongs to the people of Israel.
A native-born person must prepare these offerings in this way.
He must do this when he brings an offering made by fire.
This offering is a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
passages.original: כָּל־ הָאֶזְרָ֥ח יַעֲשֶׂה־ כָּ֖כָה אֶת־ אֵ֑לֶּה לְהַקְרִ֛יב אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: And for the generations to come, if a foreigner residing with you or someone else among you wants to prepare an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do exactly as you do.
passages.sermon:
A foreigner may live among you.
This foreigner may live with you for many generations.
Someone else may also live among you.
This person may want to prepare an offering.
The offering is made by fire.
The offering is a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The foreigner or the other person must follow your example.
He must do exactly as you do.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָגוּר֩ אִתְּכֶ֨ם גֵּ֜ר א֤וֹ אֲשֶֽׁר־ בְּתֽוֹכְכֶם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם וְעָשָׂ֛ה אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשׂ֖וּ כֵּ֥ן יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

passages.text: The assembly is to have the same statute both for you and for the foreign resident; it is a permanent statute for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God gave a law to the Israelites.
God also gave this law to the foreigners living among them.
This law is for the whole assembly.
This law is the same for Israelites and for foreigners.
This law will never change.
This law will last for all generations.
God sees Israelites and foreigners the same way.
Both Israelites and foreigners stand equal before the LORD.
passages.original: הַקָּהָ֕ל חֻקָּ֥ה אַחַ֛ת לָכֶ֖ם וְלַגֵּ֣ר הַגָּ֑ר חֻקַּ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם כָּכֶ֛ם כַּגֵּ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: The same law and the same ordinance will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing with you.”
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel.
God also included foreigners who lived with Israel.
God said, “You must have one law.”
This law is for you, the Israelites.
This law is also for the foreigner who lives among you.
You and the foreigner must follow the same rule.
You and the foreigner must obey the same command.
passages.original: תּוֹרָ֥ה אַחַ֛ת וּמִשְׁפָּ֥ט אֶחָ֖ד יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֥ר אִתְּכֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you and you eat the food of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a message.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD said, “I am bringing you into a land.
You will enter this land because I am leading you there.
When you arrive in the land, you will eat its food.
When you eat the bread of the land, you must give an offering to the LORD.
You must lift up this offering to the LORD.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם בְּבֹֽאֲכֶם֙ אֶל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֲנִ֛י מֵבִ֥יא אֶתְכֶ֖ם שָֽׁמָּה׃ וְהָיָ֕ה בַּאֲכָלְכֶ֖ם מִלֶּ֣חֶם הָאָ֑רֶץ תָּרִ֥ימוּ תְרוּמָ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution; offer it just like an offering from the threshing floor.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave laws to the Israelites.
God commanded the Israelites to give offerings.
When you make dough, take the first part.
From the first of your dough, take a piece.
Lift up this piece as an offering to God.
This piece is a cake.
Offer this cake to God.
Offer it in the same way as you offer grain from the threshing floor.
Give this offering to God.
passages.original: רֵאשִׁית֙ עֲרִסֹ֣תֵכֶ֔ם חַלָּ֖ה תָּרִ֣ימוּ תְרוּמָ֑ה כִּתְרוּמַ֣ת גֹּ֔רֶן כֵּ֖ן תָּרִ֥ימוּ אֹתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to the Israelites.
God said, “Give an offering to the LORD from the first of your dough.
Do this in every generation.
Give this offering whenever you make bread.
Give it to the LORD as a gift.
Continue this practice for all your descendants.”
passages.original: מֵרֵאשִׁית֙ עֲרִסֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם תִּתְּנ֥וּ לַיהוָ֖ה תְּרוּמָ֑ה לְדֹרֹ֖תֵיכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: Now if you stray unintentionally and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses— all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the LORD gave them and continuing through the generations to come— and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the regulation, and one male goat as a sin offering.
passages.sermon:
God gave commandments to Israel through Moses.
God gave these commandments from the day He spoke to Moses.
These commandments continue for all generations.
If the people of Israel stray by mistake,
If they do not obey all these commandments,
If the congregation does not know about the mistake,
Then the whole congregation must act.
They must bring one young bull as a burnt offering to the LORD.
This offering will have a pleasing smell to the LORD.
They must also bring the bull’s grain offering and drink offering as the law requires.
They must bring one male goat as a sin offering.
passages.original: וְכִ֣י תִשְׁגּ֔וּ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲשׂ֔וּ אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַמִּצְוֺ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃ אֵת֩ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּיַד־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה מִן־ הַיּ֞וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר צִוָּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה וָהָ֖לְאָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃ וְהָיָ֗ה אִ֣ם מֵעֵינֵ֣י הָעֵדָה֮ נֶעֶשְׂתָ֣ה לִשְׁגָגָה֒ וְעָשׂ֣וּ כָל־ הָעֵדָ֡ה פַּ֣ר בֶּן־ בָּקָר֩ אֶחָ֨ד לְעֹלָ֜ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיחֹ֙חַ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּמִנְחָת֥וֹ וְנִסְכּ֖וֹ כַּמִּשְׁפָּ֑ט וּשְׂעִיר־ עִזִּ֥ים אֶחָ֖ד לְחַטָּֽת׃

passages.text: The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional and they have brought to the LORD an offering made by fire and a sin offering, presented before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
passages.sermon:
The priest makes atonement for the whole congregation of Israel.
The people of Israel have sinned unintentionally.
The people bring their offering to the LORD.
They bring an offering made by fire to the LORD.
They also bring a sin offering before the LORD.
They bring these offerings because of their unintentional sin.
The LORD forgives them.
passages.original: וְכִפֶּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עַֽל־ כָּל־ עֲדַ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְנִסְלַ֣ח לָהֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ שְׁגָגָ֣ה הִ֔וא וְהֵם֩ הֵבִ֨יאוּ אֶת־ קָרְבָּנָ֜ם אִשֶּׁ֣ה לַֽיהוָ֗ה וְחַטָּאתָ֛ם לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עַל־ שִׁגְגָתָֽם׃

passages.text: Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Israel through Moses.
Sometimes the people of Israel make mistakes.
Sometimes they do not obey all of God's commandments.
Sometimes these mistakes happen without meaning to.
Sometimes the whole congregation sins by accident.
Sometimes foreigners live among the people of Israel.
If all the people sin unintentionally, God provides a way for forgiveness.
God will forgive the whole congregation of Israel.
God will also forgive the foreigners living among them.
God forgives because the sin was unintentional.
God's forgiveness is for everyone who sinned by mistake.
passages.original: וְנִסְלַ֗ח לְכָל־ עֲדַת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם כִּ֥י לְכָל־ הָעָ֖ם בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Also, if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
passages.sermon:
One person may sin by mistake.
This sin is unintentional.
That person must bring an offering to God.
The offering must be a female goat.
The goat must be one year old.
This goat is for a sin offering.
passages.original: וְאִם־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ אַחַ֖ת תֶּחֱטָ֣א בִשְׁגָגָ֑ה וְהִקְרִ֛יבָה עֵ֥ז בַּת־ שְׁנָתָ֖הּ לְחַטָּֽאת׃

passages.text: And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the person who erred by sinning unintentionally; and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
passages.sermon:
A priest serves the people of Israel.
A person may sin by mistake.
This person did not mean to sin.
The priest brings an offering for this person.
The priest stands before the LORD.
The priest makes atonement for the person who sinned by mistake.
God accepts the atonement.
God forgives the person.
passages.original: וְכִפֶּ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֗ן עַל־ הַנֶּ֧פֶשׁ הַשֹּׁגֶ֛גֶת בְּחֶטְאָ֥ה בִשְׁגָגָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָ֖יו וְנִסְלַ֥ח לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to the people of Israel.
Some people were born Israelites.
Some people were foreigners living among the Israelites.
God said one law must apply to everyone who sins by mistake.
This law is the same for native-born Israelites and for foreigners living with them.
Everyone who acts in error must follow this one law.
passages.original: הָֽאֶזְרָח֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְלַגֵּ֖ר הַגָּ֣ר בְּתוֹכָ֑ם תּוֹרָ֤ה אַחַת֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֔ם לָעֹשֶׂ֖ה בִּשְׁגָגָֽה׃

passages.text: But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That person shall be cut off from among his people.
passages.sermon:
A person may sin defiantly.
This person acts with a high hand.
This person may be a native-born Israelite.
This person may be a foreigner living among the Israelites.
This person blasphemes the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The person who blasphemes the LORD must be cut off.
This person will be separated from his people.
passages.original: וְהַנֶּ֜פֶשׁ אֲשֶֽׁר־ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה׀ בְּיָ֣ד רָמָ֗ה מִן־ הָֽאֶזְרָח֙ וּמִן־ הַגֵּ֔ר אֶת־ יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא מְגַדֵּ֑ף וְנִכְרְתָ֛ה הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא מִקֶּ֥רֶב עַמָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.”
passages.sermon:
This person has despised the word of the LORD.
He has broken the LORD’s commandment.
This person will certainly be cut off from the people.
His guilt remains on him.
passages.original: כִּ֤י דְבַר־ יְהוָה֙ בָּזָ֔ה וְאֶת־ מִצְוָת֖וֹ הֵפַ֑ר הִכָּרֵ֧ת׀ תִּכָּרֵ֛ת הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַהִ֖וא עֲוֺנָ֥ה בָֽהּ׃פ

passages.text: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites lived in the wilderness.
They found a man.
The man gathered wood.
He gathered wood on the Sabbath day.
passages.original: וַיִּהְי֥וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אִ֛ישׁ מְקֹשֵׁ֥שׁ עֵצִ֖ים בְּי֥וֹם הַשַּׁבָּֽת׃

passages.text: Those who found the man gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation, and because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody.
passages.sermon:
Some Israelites found a man.
The man was gathering wood.
This happened on the Sabbath day.
The Israelites who found him brought him to Moses.
They also brought him to Aaron.
They brought him to the whole congregation of Israel.
No one knew what should be done to the man.
The people had not received instructions for this situation.
They placed the man in custody.
They waited to learn what should be done with him.
passages.original: וַיַּקְרִ֣יבוּ אֹת֔וֹ הַמֹּצְאִ֥ים אֹת֖וֹ מְקֹשֵׁ֣שׁ עֵצִ֑ים אֶל־ מֹשֶׁה֙ וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאֶ֖ל כָּל־ הָעֵדָֽה׃ וַיַּנִּ֥יחוּ אֹת֖וֹ בַּמִּשְׁמָ֑ר כִּ֚י לֹ֣א פֹרַ֔שׁ מַה־ יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave a command.
The LORD said the man must die.
The man had gathered wood on the Sabbath.
The LORD said the whole congregation must stone the man.
They must stone him with stones.
They must do this outside the camp.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה מ֥וֹת יוּמַ֖ת הָאִ֑ישׁ רָג֨וֹם אֹת֤וֹ בָֽאֲבָנִים֙ כָּל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: So the whole congregation took the man outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
passages.sermon:
The whole congregation took the man.
They led him outside the camp.
They stoned him with stones.
He died.
They did this because the LORD had commanded Moses.
passages.original: וַיֹּצִ֨יאוּ אֹת֜וֹ כָּל־ הָעֵדָ֗ה אֶל־ מִחוּץ֙ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֔ה וַיִּרְגְּמ֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ בָּאֲבָנִ֖ים וַיָּמֹ֑ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־ מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

passages.text: Later, the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout the generations to come they are to make for themselves tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD told Moses to give the Israelites instructions.
The Israelites must make tassels for themselves.
They must attach these tassels to the corners of their garments.
They must do this for all their generations.
They must put a blue cord on each tassel at the corner.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־ בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם וְעָשׂ֨וּ לָהֶ֥ם צִיצִ֛ת עַל־ כַּנְפֵ֥י בִגְדֵיהֶ֖ם לְדֹרֹתָ֑ם וְנָֽתְנ֛וּ עַל־ צִיצִ֥ת הַכָּנָ֖ף פְּתִ֥יל תְּכֵֽלֶת׃

passages.text: These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD, that you may obey them and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave a command to the Israelites.
God told them to make tassels for the corners of their garments.
God said to put a blue cord on each tassel.
These tassels will be for you to see.
When you see the tassels, you will remember all the commandments of the LORD.
You will do all the commandments.
You must not follow your own heart.
You must not follow your own eyes.
You must not turn away from God’s ways.
You must not act unfaithfully by following your own desires.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֣ה לָכֶם֮ לְצִיצִת֒ וּרְאִיתֶ֣ם אֹת֗וֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ מִצְוֺ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֹתָ֑ם וְלֹֽא־ תָתֻ֜רוּ אַחֲרֵ֤י לְבַבְכֶם֙ וְאַחֲרֵ֣י עֵֽינֵיכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־ אַתֶּ֥ם זֹנִ֖ים אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the Israelites through Moses.
God gave them commandments.
God wanted them to remember His commandments.
God wanted them to obey all His commandments.
If they obeyed, they would be holy.
They would be holy to their God.
passages.original: לְמַ֣עַן תִּזְכְּר֔וּ וַעֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם אֶת־ כָּל־ מִצְוֺתָ֑י וִהְיִיתֶ֥ם קְדֹשִׁ֖ים לֵֽאלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD is your God.
The LORD brought you out of the land of Egypt.
The LORD did this to be your God.
The LORD is your God.
passages.original: אֲנִ֞י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֤אתִי אֶתְכֶם֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לִהְי֥וֹת לָכֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִ֑ים אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃פ
